chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man performs one prayer completely, all of his prayers are accepted, even if they are not complete; and if he spoils all of them, nothing is accepted from him, nor is an optional prayer or an obligatory one reckoned for him; and indeed, the optional prayer is only accepted after the acceptance of the obligatory prayer; and when the man does not perform the obligatory prayer, the optional prayer is not accepted from him, and the optional prayer is made only to complete what was spoiled of the obligatory prayer.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the acceptance of optional prayers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores the hierarchical dependency of supererogatory prayers (nafilah) on the validity of obligatory ones (fardh), a principle often cited to explain why neglected fardh prayers invalidate subsequent nafilah. It highlights the pedagogical purpose of nafilah as a means to rectify minor defects in obligatory acts, reinforcing the concept that spiritual merit is built upon a solid foundation of duty. This view aligns with the Shia emphasis on the integrity of the primary worship before engaging in voluntary enhancements.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zuurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When a man completes (the rituals) of a Salāt properly, all of his other Salāt would be accepted; even though those may not be complete; and if he spoils all of them, nothing would be Accepted from these, and they would not be Reckoned for him, neither an optional nor an Obligatory one; and rather, an optional is (only accepted) after the Acceptance of the Obligatory (Salāt). And when the man does not fulfil the Obligatory (Salāt), the optional one would not be Accepted from him; and rather, they are to complete therewith the shortcomings of the obligatory ones.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

When a man completes one Salah (prayer) properly, all of his other prayers are accepted; even though they may not be complete. If he loses them, altogether, none of his Salah (prayer) is accepted, and not even his optional or obligatory prayers are counted. Optional Salah (prayer) are accepted only after obligatory prayers are accepted. If one does not perform obligatory prayers, optional prayers are not accepted; they are to complete therewith the shortcomings of the obligatory ones.”
